items.title: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI
items.excerpt: The Verge reports that Musk, Benioff, Huang and now Microsoft's Satya Nadella have adopted the White House's 'super intelligence' terminology in place of 'AI'. Political-communication angle on the administration's AI rebrand; dedup note: related to the SIF/rename thread from 10-08 to 10-11, and it reports corporate adoption rather than a new government decision.

items.title: These Midterm Races Will Decide Data Centers’ Political Fate
items.excerpt: WIRED reports that in Senate and governor races across the US, candidates are trying to outdo each other in opposing AI data centers, which makes datacenter siting a midterm campaign issue. Note: this is election-analysis reporting, so avoid horse-race framing.

items.title: ICE Emails Discuss Using Palantir-Supported Tool to Investigate Voter Fraud
items.excerpt: According to FOIA documents published by Democracy Forward, ICE looked into feeding voter-roll data into ELITE, a Palantir-supported targeting tool normally used to identify people for deportation. Borderline on relevance: the tool is data analytics, and AI is not central to the headline. It is also about 71h old, at the edge of the window.

items.title: The US and China Cannot Slow the AI Race, But They Can Make It Safer
items.excerpt: An analysis piece arguing that the US does not need to trust China, share frontier models with it, or slow its own development to have a national-security interest in AI safety cooperation. This is commentary, not a decision.

items.title: Europe Wants to Regulate AI Friends. But How Do You Curb Dependency?
items.excerpt: Nik Roeingh writes that Europe's KIDS Act is a first step toward regulating AI companions, but that regulators are still working out how to address emotional dependency. Policy analysis of an EU rulemaking track.

items.title: At Ireland’s AI Summit, Tech Industry Dominates as Civil Society Sits Out
items.excerpt: Liz Carolan reports that Ireland held an invitation-only AI summit while leading the EU Digital Omnibus negotiations (which touch AI Act implementation), and asks whose interests are represented, as civil society stayed away.

items.title: Nippon Life v. OpenAI and the Future of AI Legal Work
items.excerpt: Daniel Kalish examines the Nippon Life v. OpenAI litigation and whether chatbot-drafted legal briefs could count as 'unauthorized practice of law' under century-old licensing statutes. Analysis of a pending case. Note: the og:image is a .tif.

items.title: 서범수 "취약층 학생 12만명에 AI 지원한다더니…접속자 저조"
items.excerpt: 국민의힘 서범수 의원이 한국장학재단 자료를 인용해, 교육부가 추경 95억원으로 시작한 취약계층 고교생 유료 AI 서비스 지원사업 'AI 온이음' 실이용자가 목표 12만명의 10%에 못 미치는 8,324명이라고 밝혔다. 예산 중 28억5천만원은 반납될 예정이다. 국정감사 자료이며, 업체 선정 비판은 의원 측 주장으로 귀속해야 한다.

items.title: 글로벌 AI 허브 유치전, 충남도 뛴다…분산형 공모 가능성도 대비
items.excerpt: 과기정통부가 10월 14일 공청회를 열어 정부 '글로벌 AI 허브'(UN AI 허브) 입지 선정 기준과 절차를 안내하고 이달 중 후보지 공모를 낸다. 인천·부산·광주·경북·제주·고양에 이어 충남도도 유치전에 나섰다. 지역 유치전 기사이므로 정부의 공모 공고 자체가 더 강한 기사가 될 수 있다.

items.title: 중기부·국세청, AI 기업 2천559개사 성장·세정지원 연계
items.excerpt: 중기부와 국세청이 AI 중소·스타트업 2,559곳에 세정지원을 연계한다고 10월 11일 발표했다. 창업 5년 이내 AI 스타트업은 정기 세무조사 대상에서 빼고, 그 밖의 AI 중소기업은 신청하면 정기 세무조사를 2년 유예한다. 기간은 2026년 10월 1일부터 2028년 2월 28일까지이며, 정부 공식 발표에 근거한 기사다.

items.title: 10 Takeaways from Q3
items.excerpt: ChinaTalk's quarterly digest covers AI, China, defense, national security and supply chains. It is a broad analysis roundup with no single decision, so it is a weak pick and the curator should use it only as a fallback.
